originalTitle: The Polygamist's author says women see themselves reflected in her Netflix hit
title: Our African Super Storyteller: Sue Nyathi!
content:
Hello, amazing friends all across Africa! Are you ready for a super cool story today? It’s about a wonderful lady from our very own continent. Her name is Sue Nyathi, and she is a fantastic storyteller! She writes exciting books, and one of her books even became a TV show that lots of grown-ups watched on Netflix!

Meet Sue Nyathi: Our Storyteller Hero!

Sue comes from a beautiful country called Zimbabwe. Zimbabwe is a special place in Southern Africa. It's a land with amazing animals like elephants and giraffes roaming free. It also has very warm and friendly people who love to smile. Sue Nyathi is from this wonderful place. She is a writer, which means she tells stories using words in books. Sue loves to write stories that make people think and feel many different things. Her stories help us understand the world better and learn about other people’s lives. She puts a lot of heart into every word she writes. Did you know? Zimbabwe is famous for Victoria Falls! It's one of the biggest and most beautiful waterfalls in the whole world. It's so big, you can hear the water roaring from far, far away!

Her Big Story on TV!

Sue wrote a very special book. It is called "The Polygamist." When people read this book, they loved it so much! Then, something super exciting happened. This amazing book became a popular TV show! The show was put on Netflix. Do you know what Netflix is? It's like a magic box or a special app that lets you watch lots of movies and TV shows right on your television, tablet, or phone. It has stories from all over the world! Many grown-up ladies watched the show that came from Sue's book. They said things like, "Hey, that's just like me!" or "I feel like I've been through something similar!" They saw their own lives, their own feelings, and their own experiences in Sue's story. This made the show very, very special to them. Did you know? Watching stories can help us learn about different people, different cultures, and even different feelings! It’s like traveling without leaving your home!

How Did Her Book Get Printed?

When Sue first wrote "The Polygamist," she really, really wanted to share it with everyone. She knew it was a good story and that people would enjoy it. But sometimes, getting a book printed, put into covers, and then sold in shops costs a lot of money. It’s a big job! So, Sue did something super brave and very clever! She used her *own* money to pay for her first book to be printed. This special way of doing things is called "self-funding." It means she was her own helper, using her savings to make her dream come true. Imagine saving up your pocket money to buy all the paper, ink, and covers for a giant book all by yourself! That’s what Sue did, in a way, for her first big story. It took a lot of hard work and belief in herself. Did you know? The very first books were not printed at all! They were written by hand by special people called scribes, sometimes taking many months or even years to finish just one book!

Is Writing a Story Hard?

Sue Nyathi is a super writer, and she loves telling stories. But she also thinks about other people who want to write books. She wonders, "Is it too expensive for everyone to share their stories?" This is a very important question to ask. Why is it important? Because every person has a story to tell! Every voice matters. Imagine if only people with lots and lots of money could write and publish books. We would miss out on so many amazing tales! We wouldn't hear stories from different villages, different cities, and different people all across Africa and the world. It would be like having only one kind of fruit to eat when there are so many delicious and colorful fruits in the world! We need all kinds of stories, just like we need all kinds of fruits. Did you know? Storytelling has been a super important part of African culture for thousands of years! Grandparents and elders have passed down amazing tales, fables, and histories from one generation to the next, often around a warm fire!

Why Are Stories So Important?

Stories are like magic! They help us learn new things about the world and about ourselves. They help us imagine new worlds and new adventures in our minds. They also help us understand how other people feel, even if they are very different from us. When grown-up women saw themselves in Sue's story on Netflix, it made them feel seen and understood. It showed them that their own experiences, their own joys, and their own challenges are important and worth sharing. Stories can make us laugh, make us think, and sometimes even make us a little bit sad. But they always make us feel something! Did you know? When you read a story, your brain is like a super amazing movie projector! It imagines all the characters, places, and actions, making the story come alive inside your head!

What Can You Do?

You might be a young storyteller too! Maybe you already tell exciting tales to your friends or your family. You can also draw pictures and make up amazing adventures in your imagination. And one of the best things you can do is to read lots and lots of books! Visit your school library, or ask a grown-up to read to you. Every time you read a book, you help a writer's dream come true, just like Sue Nyathi's dream. Who knows? Maybe one day, you will write a super story too! You could write about your life, your village, or amazing adventures! Did you know? The more you read, the better you become at writing and telling your *own* stories! Reading helps your brain grow strong and full of ideas!

Sue's Amazing Message

Sue Nyathi, our wonderful storyteller from Zimbabwe, reminds us that sharing stories is very, very important for everyone. It might be hard sometimes, like paying for your own books, but it's always worth it in the end. Her incredible journey, from writing her book with her own money to seeing it become a popular TV show, teaches us a big lesson. It shows us that if you have a dream, work hard, and believe in your story, amazing things can happen! So let's keep reading, keep writing, and keep sharing our wonderful African stories with the whole world! Everyone has a story inside them, and every story deserves to be heard!
summary: Sue Nyathi, a writer from Zimbabwe, used her own money to publish her first book, "The Polygamist," which later became a popular TV show on Netflix, making many women feel their own lives were reflected in the story.
whyMatters: This story matters because it shows us that everyone has important stories to tell, even if it's hard to share them, and that African writers like Sue Nyathi can share amazing stories that are loved all over the world.

title: A Story About Peace from Far Away Lands
content:
Hello, Amazing Kids!

Hello, my wonderful friends across Africa! It's your kid-friendly news reporter here. Today, we are going to talk about something happening very, very far away from us. It's in a part of the world called Europe. Sometimes, even far away, we hear news that makes us think about peace and being kind to one another. Let's learn together in a gentle way. We will talk about two countries called Russia and Ukraine.

Where Are Russia and Ukraine?

Imagine looking at a big, colourful map of the whole world! Can you see Africa? Yes, you can! Now, if you travel very far north from Africa, across a big sea, you will find a different land. That's where Russia and Ukraine are. They are neighbours. This means their homes are very close to each other, just like your house might be close to your friend's house. They are big countries with lots of towns, forests, and rivers. Did you know? Russia is the biggest country in the whole world! It's so big that it stretches across two continents: Europe and Asia. Ukraine is also a very big country, much bigger than many countries you might know!

What's Happening There?

Sometimes, even good friends can have big disagreements. They might want different things, or they might not understand each other very well. That is a little bit like what is happening between Russia and Ukraine. They have had a big disagreement for a while now. This disagreement means that sometimes, things become very noisy and sad. People in both countries wish for things to be calm and peaceful. Did you know? When people have disagreements, talking can help a lot! Sometimes, grown-ups try to talk and listen to each other to find a way to be friends again.

When Things Get Loud

Recently, something happened that made many people sad. From Ukraine, some things were sent towards a place in Russia called Moscow. Moscow is like the main big city in Russia. When these things arrived, they caused loud noises and some buildings got hurt. It was not a happy day for the people there. Some people got hurt, and that is very sad for everyone. Then, from Russia, some things were also sent towards Ukraine. They went to a very important city in Ukraine called Kyiv. Kyiv is the main big city in Ukraine. When these things landed, they also caused loud noises. Some buildings in Kyiv started to burn a little bit, like when you have a small campfire, but it was much bigger and not a happy kind of fire. This made people in Kyiv feel scared and sad too. Everyone wants their homes to be safe and sound. Did you know? There are special people called firefighters who are very brave! When fires start, they rush to help put them out and keep everyone safe. They are real heroes!

People Want Peace

When things like this happen, it makes many people around the world feel sad. Children, just like you, in Russia and Ukraine, wish for playtime and school without any worries. They want to hug their families and feel safe. Grown-ups in both countries also want peace. They want to be able to go to work and take care of their families without any loud noises or worries. Peace means everyone can live happily and safely together. Did you know? The symbol for peace is often a white dove! A dove is a beautiful bird that looks very gentle. Sometimes, people draw doves to show they want peace in the world.

What Can We Do?

Even though Russia and Ukraine are very far away, we can still do something. We can think about them and wish for peace. We can draw pictures of peace, with happy sunshine and people holding hands. We can also remember to be extra kind to our friends and neighbours here in Africa. When we are kind to each other, we are helping to make our own small corner of the world a peaceful place. Every little bit of kindness helps the world shine brighter. Did you know? There is a special day called the International Day of Peace! On this day, people all over the world think about how we can all live together without fighting. It happens every year on September 21st.

Let's Keep Hoping for Peace!

So, remember, my dear friends. When there are big disagreements, it can make things loud and sad. But many, many people want things to be peaceful again. Countries around the world are trying to help Russia and Ukraine talk to each other and find a way to be friendly neighbours. Just like when you and your friend make up after an argument, it feels much better when everyone is happy and calm. Let's keep hoping and wishing for peace for all the children and grown-ups in Russia and Ukraine. We believe in a world where everyone can live safely and happily. Did you know? Children all over the world send messages of peace to each other. They draw pictures, write songs, and share ideas about how to make the world a better, kinder place for everyone. Your drawings and kind thoughts can travel far!
summary: Recently, two countries far away, Russia and Ukraine, had a big disagreement that caused some sadness and damage in their main cities, but many people are hoping for peace and kindness to return.
whyMatters: It's important because when countries disagree, people can get sad or hurt, and everyone wants children and families to be safe and happy in their homes.
